documents.unit: Center for Effective Teaching and Learning (CETL)
documents.title: Recommendations for Teaching & Learning with AI
documents.stance_why: The page sets no campus rule on AI use. It says the academic honesty policy is "under revision to include AI" and that "it is good idea to develop your own AI policy", offering three templates (ban, encourage, "somewhere in between"). Because the decision is handed to instructors with tiered templates, the stance is delegates.
tiers: encourage the use of AI in all circumstances
documents.summary: Teaching-center guidance for faculty on writing a course AI policy, with three advice templates (ban, embrace, in between). It also covers handling suspected misuse, why AI detectors are unreliable and not enabled on campus, assignment redesign, and classroom activities using AI.

units.why: Frames the guidance: LLMs are "disrupting the workforce", so CETL "recommends that faculty approach AI in a thoughtful and nuanced manner". It is a recommendation setting the purpose of the page, so the framework type P56.
units.anchor: CETL recommends that faculty approach AI in a thoughtful and nuanced manner

units.why: States that LLMs are "disrupting the workforce by providing increased productivity", a career-relevance rationale for engaging with AI, so P44.
units.anchor: disrupting the workforce by providing increased productivity
units.frag_start: AI Large Language Models, such as

units.why: Says misuse of AI "generally falls under standards regarding plagiarism and the misrepresentation of work": improper AI use is handled as academic dishonesty, P36.
units.anchor: misuse of AI generally falls under standards regarding plagiarism and the misrepresentation of work

units.why: States the academic honesty policy "is under revision to include AI": the policy is provisional and being updated, so P54.
units.anchor: academic honesty policy is under revision to include AI

units.why: Advises "it is good idea to develop your own AI policy" because of confusion about AI; the course rule is left to each instructor, so P04. P09 does not fit because this is a recommendation, not a syllabus mandate.
units.anchor: it is good idea to develop your own AI policy

units.why: For faculty who "oppose all use of AI", advises they identify their "wholesale ban of AI"; this is the ban tier of three offered, so P05 rather than a campus default P01.
units.anchor: Identify your wholesale ban of AI.

units.why: Banning faculty should explain how AI "can lead to the deterioration of hard-earned skills": a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: how use of AI can lead to the deterioration of hard-earned skills
units.frag_start: Explain why you think this ban

units.why: Banning faculty should "Identify (with examples) the specific consequences of misuse": penalties stated in advance, P37.
units.anchor: Identify (with examples) the specific consequences of misuse.

units.why: Banning faculty should "Link back to the broader Cal State LA academic honesty policy", tying course rules to the campus integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: Link back to the broader Cal State LA
units.policy: Faculty who ban AI should link the course AI policy back to the broader Cal State LA academic honesty policy.

units.why: Describes faculty who "encourage the use of AI in all circumstances"; this is the encourage tier of three offered, so P05 rather than a campus default P02.
units.anchor: Faculty who encourage the use of AI in all circumstances would be advised to

units.why: Encouraging faculty should "Identify (with examples) how AI might be used": stating permitted uses to students, so P09 (state expectations in the syllabus).
units.anchor: Identify (with examples) how AI might be used.

units.why: Encouraging faculty should "Explain why you think the embrace of AI is important to the work you are doing": a rationale for AI use, closest to P44.
units.anchor: Explain why you think the embrace of AI is important
units.frag_start: Explain why you think the embrace

units.why: Says to explain that AI "plagiarizes from copyrighted sources, shows bias, makes things up" and that tools "should be fact-checked"; the verification duty is the load-bearing point, so P31.
units.anchor: these tools should be fact-checked and used with careful deliberation

units.why: Says "the student, not the AI, will be responsible for any errors": student accountability for submitted work, P29.
units.anchor: the student, not the AI, will be responsible for any errors

units.why: Encouraging faculty should "Clarify (and demand) that students cite AI tools" with references and in-text citations: citation requirement, P24 (P25 not chosen as no prompt or output details are specified).
units.anchor: Clarify (and demand) that students
units.policy: Faculty should clarify and demand that students cite AI tools with both references and in-text citations.

units.why: Says "Be prepared to teach students how to use AI for respective coursework": instructors teach AI use as a skill, P44.
units.anchor: Be prepared to teach students how to use AI for respective coursework.

units.why: Middle-ground faculty should "Identify (with examples) the uses and times you consider AI appropriate" and inappropriate: the in-between tier with uses spelled out, P05.
units.anchor: Identify (with examples) the uses and times you consider AI appropriate

units.why: Middle-ground faculty should "Explain why you think your expectations are important": communicating expectations and reasons, P09.
units.anchor: Explain why you think your expectations are important to the work you are doing.

units.why: Middle-ground faculty should "Explain that use of AI can lead to the deterioration of hard-earned skills": skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Explain that use of AI can lead to the deterioration of hard-earned skills.

units.why: Middle-ground faculty should also "Identify (with examples) the specific consequences of misuse": penalties in advance, P37. Coded separately because it belongs to a different tier.
units.anchor: Identify (with examples) the specific consequences of misuse.

units.why: Middle-ground faculty should demand students "cite AI tools (when allowed)": citation of permitted AI use, P24.
units.anchor: cite AI tools (when allowed) with both references and in-text citations.

units.why: Suggests "Consider allowing student to co-create their policy so that there is greater student buy in": a way of setting the course rule that no type covers, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Consider allowing student to co-create their policy
units.uncovered_note: Instructors may let students co-create the course AI policy to increase student buy-in.

units.why: Points to San Francisco State sample syllabus statements (prohibition, transparency, incorporation); this is a set of tiered templates, P05.
units.anchor: include three sample policy statements, one focused on prohibition, one focused on transparency
units.frag_start: San Francisco State recommendations on AI Syllabus Policies
units.policy: San Francisco State recommendations on AI Syllabus Policies include three sample policy statements, one focused on prohibition, one on transparency, one on incorporation and critical AI.

units.why: Says that if instructors use AI to draft their policy, "tell your students. It's only fair": instructor disclosure of own AI use, P47.
units.anchor: But if you use them, tell your students.

units.why: Says AI tools "can help you draft your policy": instructors may use AI for drafting syllabus policy, P59.
units.anchor: can help you draft your policy

units.why: Directs faculty to CSU systemwide "Guidelines for Faculty Regarding AI in Instruction", which have recommendations for instructors who allow or prohibit AI: points to a system-level framework, P56.
units.anchor: Guidelines for Faculty Regarding AI in Instruction
units.policy: Systemwide Academic Senate guidelines for faculty regarding AI in instruction are on the CSU AI Commons.

units.why: Advises to "reward processes over products" and use rubrics not rewarding work AI could do alone as the best way to prevent misuse: grading redesigned around AI, P35.
units.anchor: reward processes over products, and to use rubrics that do not reward work
units.frag_start: The best way to prevent such misuse is to

units.why: The sample rubric includes an "AI Level (50%) = F" column, so work an AI could produce without human help earns an F: grading scheme redesigned around AI, P35.
units.anchor: AI Level (50%) = F
units.policy: A sample rubric has an "AI Level" column in which work that AI could do without human assistance earns 50% and an F.

units.why: For suspected misuse, says "Have a conversation with the student" and ask specific questions before proceeding: talk with the student before escalating, P57.
units.anchor: Have a conversation with the student. Ask specific questions about the assignment.
units.frag_start: Have a conversation with the student.
units.frag_end: probe deeper to find out what happened.

units.why: Says to review the submission, "especially citations, which AI frequently invents", as evidence of misuse: examining the work for signs of AI, P40.
units.anchor: Review the submission well (especially citations, which AI frequently invents).

units.why: Says to "Proceed based on the expectations of the AI policy you've created": sanctions follow the instructor-written policy, P04.
units.anchor: Proceed based on the expectations of the AI policy

units.why: Says instructors "really can't" detect AI use with certainty and that detectors "both under- and over-identify writing": detectors unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: AI detection tools, but they both under- and over-identify writing

units.why: Lists that detectors "Identified original student writing as having been written by an LLM" among their failings: unreliability, P39.
units.anchor: Identified original student writing as having been written by an LLM

units.why: Lists that detectors "Shared both the faculty members' data and the data of students", a data-sharing concern; P50 (protect data) fits better than P39 since the point is privacy.
units.anchor: Shared both the faculty members' data and the data of students

units.why: Says detectors "Created an LLM arms race that shifts faculty attention from teaching to policing LLM use": a reason not to rely on them, P39.
units.anchor: shifts faculty attention from teaching to policing LLM use

units.why: Says "the campus does not have plans to separately purchase the AI detection feature in Turnitin": the institution declines to use a detector, P39.
units.anchor: the campus does not have plans to separately purchase the AI detection feature in Turnitin

units.why: Cites detector "bias against non-native English writers" increasing false positives for "already marginalized learners": an equity reason against detectors, P39 (P53 is about AI itself).
units.anchor: AI detectors are susceptible to bias against non-native English writers
units.frag_start: indicated that AI detectors are susceptible

units.why: The CSU Directors statement says detecting AI content "is currently not 100% reliable" and the instructor cannot "prove" a case: detector reliability, P39.
units.anchor: the ability to detect AI-generated content is currently not 100% reliable

units.why: The CSU statement suggests "clear communication about expectations related to AI use for assignments and assessments via course syllabi and assignment instructions": P09.
units.anchor: clear communication about expectations related to AI use for assignments and assessments

units.why: Suggests to "Get an in-person writing sample the first week of class so you establish a baseline": assignment redesign to counter AI, P35.
units.anchor: Get an in-person writing sample the first week of class so you establish a baseline.

units.why: Suggests to "Require students to maintain a detailed revision history" of their writing; keeping drafts as process evidence is closest to P26 (keep and submit drafts), though it is not stated as submitted.
units.anchor: Require students to maintain a detailed revision history of their writing

units.why: Suggests "work that is presented live or that must be performed, such as a live Q & A": understanding checked through live performance, P34.

units.frag_start: Assign work that is presented live

units.why: Suggests "Personalize the assignment so students must incorporate their own experience", an AI-resistant redesign, P35.
units.anchor: Personalize the assignment so students must incorporate their own experience.

units.why: Says assignments AI cannot do now "may be easy for AI to complete next semester": the advice is provisional, P54.
units.anchor: may be easy for AI to complete next semester
